children: Search is how you find a Document in Barkpark — two engines behind one contract, tuned for relevance and self-correcting from clicks.

The default engine is Postgres Search, built on a generated Search Vector with BM25F-style field weighting (title weighted above body). The alternative is the Indx Engine, a retriever seam that swaps in via engine=indx without changing the caller (see Indx Retriever Seam). Both answer the same query contract exposed through Search Intelligence on the HTTP API v1.

Results carry Search Facets for drill-down. When a query misspells a term, Did You Mean offers a correction, and Synonyms expand known equivalents. The Auto Correction Loop closes the feedback circuit — it learns from click signal (the canonical example: hadless → headless) so the index improves itself over time.

Search quality is pinned by Golden Eval, a fixed query/expected-result set run as a regression gate so a relevance tweak can't silently regress. The same content that feeds search is what the Edge Extractor mines for the Content Graph — search and graph are two reads of one corpus, which is why a Search note bridges naturally to Graph Traversal.
